content.title: About
content.content: A turkey sandwich on wheat bread consists of sliced turkey, fresh vegetables, lettuce, and a light sauce placed between two pieces of whole‑grain wheat bread. It is a balanced snack rich in protein and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is one of the leanest meats, low in saturated fat.
Wheat bread provides slow‑release carbohydrates, helping maintain energy levels.
The sandwich is a common “school lunch” item in the United States.
Adding fresh veggies boosts vitamins A and C content.
It is portable and does not require reheating.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Turkey supplies high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, turkey contains less saturated fat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: Fiber from whole grain
items.content: Wheat bread adds dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey and whole‑grain bread are good sources of B6 and B12, supporting the nervous system.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The sandwich provides iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and processed turkey can be high in salt.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage of turkey may allow growth of pathogens such as salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. You can add mustard, hummus, or a light yogurt sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, separate the ingredients and store them individually.
